defect_observations: finite-probability.tex lines 12-15 describe the chapter as developing 'the finite part of the discrete treatment' of G&S secs 1.2, 4.1 and 6.1. Some finite items there are not presented in this chapter: the odds-to-probability inverse p = r/(r+s) and the betting reading of Definition 1.4; tree measures; Monty Hall; Example 4.15 binomial law; the fair-game (martingale) notion of Example 6.15; the historical remarks. They were not counted as gaps because no required component names them and the author scope record could not be consulted. The lead should check them against that record.

finite-probability.tex lines 401-407 define E[X|B] as an outcome sum under p_B. G&S Definition 6.2's value-sum form sum_j x_j P(X = x_j | F) is not displayed; it follows from the grouping identity (line 371) applied to the mass function p_B.

finite-probability.tex lines 171-174 require nonempty partition members. G&S Theorem 1.3 allows any pairwise disjoint cover; the empty-member case follows from finite additivity (thm:p15-finite-probability-laws item 2).

conditioning-independence-and-information-w02b-p15-006.tex lines 7-12 say Durrett gives the infinite-collection rule 'after defining independence for finitely many' objects; on p. 44 that sentence precedes the n-object definitions (only the two-object definitions on p. 43 precede it). Source-description wording only.

independent-random-variables.tex line 400 asserts that the extension's measurable-space hypotheses 'remain essential'; no counterexample or citation supports necessity on the route (Durrett p. 53 attributes counterexamples to Andersen and Jessen 1948 and Wegner 1973). The promised chapters are complete, so this does not change C016.
The lemma label thm:p15-w02c-p15-006-lambda-class (body line 198, annex line 149) carries a w02c tag inside the w02b host file. Naming only.
